newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 19.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English monarch CHARLES I, who lost his head after the Civil War, was born in 1600.
The French diplomat who supervised the building of the Suez canal Viscomte FERDINAND DE LESSEPS was born in 1805.
Australian barrister WALTER COLDHAM was born in 1860 and became a renowned legal wit.
American senator and archaeologist HIRAM BIRMINGHAM, who discovered the lost Inca city of Machu Picchu in Peru, was born in 1875.
Australian Catholic Church leader CARDINAL Sir JAMES FREEMAN was born in 1907.
Indian politician and prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1984 INDIRA GANDHI was born in 1917.
American fashion designer CALVIN KLEIN was born in 1942.
American alto-saxophonist and pianist FRED LIPSIUS, who was with 'Blood, Sweat and Tears' from 1968 until 1972, was born in 1944.
American actress JODIE FOSTER, who won an Oscar for her role in "The Silence Of The Lambs", was born in 1962.
** EVENTS **
1620 : The Pilgrim fathers in the "Mayflower" anchored at
Cape Cod two months after setting sail from Plymouth. The 87 members of a separatist Protestant sect intended to make a new life in America.
1703 : The "man in the iron mask", a prisoner in the
Bastille prison in Paris, died. His true identity was the cause of much intrigue and is celebrated in the literary works of Francois Voltaire and Alexandre Dumas.
1863 : President ABRAHAM LINCOLN delivered his Gettysburg

address at the dedication of a cemetery. "Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal...." That's how the president's two minute speech began. The cemetery was where the dead of the Battle of Gettysburg were buried.
1908 : A court in St Petersburg was adjourned when the
prosecutors refused to deal with Russia's first female barrister.
1914 : Austrian and German internees rioted at a
detention camp on the Isle of Wight in Britain.
1925 : The British parliament voted for a four-month
prison sentence for drunken driving.
1934 : The state of Victoria celebrated its 100th
birthday.
1937 : Cyclist HUBERT OPPERMAN completed the Fremantle to
Sydney ride in a record 13 days, 10 hours an 11 minutes.
1942 : Soviet Red Army troops began a massive
counter-offensive against the Germans at Stalingrad.
1946 : The Australian government approved a proposal to

set up a guided missile range in Australia as a joint venture with Britain. The British selected a South Australian site and gave assurances that the rocket tests would not threaten the Aborigines living on the reserve, where the base would be located. The site was later known as the Woomera Rocket range.
1957 : Bush fires were burning in the New South Wales
Blue Mountains for their fourth consecutive day.
1961 : Three people drowned in Sydney's worst floods
since 1956.
1969 : The U.S. Apollo 12 lunar module landed on the
moon, carrying astronauts CHARLES CONRAD and ALAN BEAN.
1978 : Nine hundred members of the People's Temple
religious sect, led by JIM JONES, committed suicide by drinking soft drinks laced with cyanide. JONES died of gunshot wounds and left seven million dollars to aid 'the oppressed people of the world'.
1980 : The cliff hanger of one of the world's most

addictive TV soap opera's was revealed. The question on everyone's lips was "Who shot JR?" Numerous newspaper and magazine articles were written on the various theories about the possible culprit in the "Dallas" series. The soap opera's baddie was Kristen.
1988 : CHRISTINA ONASSIS, the daughter of Greek shipowner
ARISTOTLE ONASSIS, died.
1990 : Leaders of NATO and the Warsaw Pact declared the
end of the Cold War when they signed the Treaty on Conventional Forces in Europe, slashing their Cold War arsenals.
1994 : The U.N. Security Council authorised NATO
warplanes to strike targets in Croatia used by Serbs to launch air attacks against U.N.-designated safe areas in neighbouring Bosnia.
1995 : A suicide bomber blasted his way into the Egyptian
embassy in Islamabad, setting off a powerful explosion that killed 16 people and wounded more than 60, including diplomats.
